tips: Load Suica to Apple/Google Wallet now while you have Wi-Fi at MSP — land in Tokyo ready to tap.
Set your watch to JST on the long leg and force the sleep cycle: melatonin at 13:00 CT (≈ 4am JST).

2026-12-15.weatherAlert: Evening temps in Tokyo will drop to around 3°C. The Omoide Yokocho outdoor seating and Kabukicho neon walk will feel biting after 14 hours of A/C.
tips: Hit the konbini first for a hot canned coffee or Oden to warm up before the Shinjuku night walk.
If Ichiran has a massive line, pivot one stop north to Shin-Okubo Koreatown for KFC (Korean Fried Chicken) at midnight.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: High risk of cold, wet afternoon. Shibuya Blue Cave is an outdoor 600k LED walk along the park path that gets miserable in December rain.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Shibuya Blue Cave illumination — ~600k blue LEDs toward Yoyogi
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Miyashita Park covered rooftop + Parco + Tower Records (9 floors) absorb a full wet afternoon without surfacing.
suggestedSwap.reason: The Blue Cave illumination is entirely outdoors and crowded; rain makes it a freezing, soggy experience.

tips: Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast — if you haven't pre-booked, pivot to Mag's Park rooftop or Hikarie 11F Sky Lobby.
If the crew is jet-lagged and fading, swap the Blue Cave for an early nomihodai and crash by 23:00.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Cold snap risk. Tokyo Skytree outdoor decks and Ueno Ameyoko open-air market are exposed to biting December winds.
tips: If the Skytree queue is insane or the wind is brutal, hit the Asahi Beer Hall's 22F Sky Room next door for the same river view with a warm beer.
For the Akiba deep-divers: Super Potato → Mandarake Complex → Taito HEY is a 3-hour vortex; non-nerds can do Kanda Myojin shrine and Ueno park.
teamLab Planets requires shoes off and wading through water — wear easy slip-offs and roll your pants.
If Golden Gai feels too touristy or crowded, pivot to KITTE rooftop for a free, cinematic nightcap facing Tokyo Station.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: Coastal Kamakura and Enoshima are highly exposed to winter winds and rain. The Enoshima climb and Fuji-over-bay sunset are weather-dependent.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Enoshima onsen finish: Enospa overlooks the bay — soak with a Fuji view before the train if legs are cooked.
suggestedSwap.reason: Rain makes the Enoshima climb slippery and ruins the Fuji view; Enospa offers a warm, covered alternative with bay views.

tips: December is peak clarity for Fuji — if it's sunny, the view from Enoshima at 16:32 is a trip highlight.
If the weather turns bad, pivot to the Hokokuji bamboo temple in Kamakura for a sheltered, crowd-free Arashiyama preview.
Run the Airbnb washer during dinner so everyone lands in Kyoto with a clean kit.
If Golden Gai peaked on the 18th, pivot to Shinjuku Batting Center for $3 (¥500) of midnight swings.

2026-12-21.weatherAlert: Rain risk for Gion golden hour and Kamo River bank nightcap.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Kamo River bank — konbini cans, December stars
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Kyoto International Manga Museum — 50,000 manga, huge English wall, a school where you just sit and read. Dangerous time vortex.
suggestedSwap.reason: Sitting on the Kamo riverbank in cold December rain is miserable; the Manga Museum is a perfect indoor time vortex.

tips: Scout Nintendo Kyoto at Takashimaya (5 min from Nishiki) today, buy in Osaka — Kansai-exclusive merch exists.
For Pontocho, send two scouts to L'Escamoteur steampunk bar at 19:40 to hold the queue while the rest finish dinner.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Rain makes the Fushimi Inari mountain trails slippery and the Kiyomizu-dera wooden stage dangerously slick.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Kiyomizu-dera — the wooden stage over the valley
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Sanjusangendo — 1,001 golden Kannon statues in a 120m hall. Indoor, jaw-dropping, criminally underrated.
suggestedSwap.reason: The wooden stage and steep Sannenzaka descent are hazardous in rain; Sanjusangendo is indoor and world-class.

tips: Past Yotsutsuji at Fushimi Inari, the crowds hit zero — the full summit loop buys a deserted mountain and bragging rights.
Hit Sake Bar Yoramu (8 seats) after the onsen — say 'osusume de' and surrender to the master's picks.

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is a wind tunnel in winter rain; Iwatayama Monkey Park closes in bad weather.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Iwatayama Monkey Park — humans enter the cage
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Ryōan-ji audible: Japan's most famous rock garden, 20 min from Kinkaku-ji — 15 stones, only 14 visible from any seat. Sit with that.
suggestedSwap.reason: Monkey Park is a steep 20-min hike that closes in rain; Ryōan-ji is a profound, mostly indoor/sheltered alternative nearby.

tips: Wakakusa-yama climb is CLOSED for our entire trip (closes 2nd Sunday of Dec) — do not attempt it.
If Kyoto wakes up white, override the plan: Kinkaku-ji at opening (gold + snow = Japan's rarest photo), then Fushimi round two.

2026-12-24.crowdAlert: KFC Christmas buckets sell out fast on Christmas Eve — pre-order or send a scout by 17:30 to secure the sacred tradition.
tips: If all 8 lost the Nintendo Museum drawing, Uji still carries the morning — Byodo-in, Tsuen tea, matcha soba, river walk.
Buy Rikuro's jiggly cheesecake near Namba station for the house — buy two, they will not survive the night.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ Christmas Day will be at maximum capacity; SUPER NINTENDO WORLD timed entry will vanish within minutes of park open.
tips: Rope-drop 45 min early and sprint to Mario Kart — single-rider lines cut 60% off the wait if Express Passes didn't cover it.
If Kinopio's Café is full, Yoshi snack stand + Power-Up Band challenges still deliver the serotonin.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Miyajima Island is highly exposed to sea winds and rain; the floating torii loses its magic in a storm.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: ITSUKUSHIMA SHRINE — the torii floating in the sea
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Energy honesty: longest day of the trip. Anyone redlining skips Miyajima, does the museum unhurried, meets us at Hiroshima station.
suggestedSwap.reason: If rain hits, the ferry and torii view are miserable; the Peace Museum is deeply impactful and deserves unhurried time anyway.

tips: This is the longest day of the trip — be honest about energy levels. It's okay to skip Miyajima and do the museum slowly.
If the museum hits heavy (it will; that's the point), take a quiet walk through Shukkei-en garden 10 min from the station.

2026-12-27.weatherAlert: Midosuji Illumination is a 4km outdoor walk; cold December winds will make this brisk.
tips: 551 Horai protocol: buy butaman 4-pack from Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner — they sell out nightly and house breakfast depends on it.
If Ura-Namba was your love story, the JR Tenma standing-bar belt is tonight's sequel — izakaya density world record.
Tax-free paperwork check tonight: receipts with passports, purchases accessible — customs CAN ask on exit. 10 minutes now beats a Dec 29 panic.
Kobe beef budget fork: $22 (¥3,500) bowls and croquette stands around Sannomiya deliver 70% of the experience at 40% of the price.
Duty-free math: Japanese whisky allocations (Hibiki/Yamazaki) beat US prices badly — buy AFTER security, keep sealed for MSP re-check.
If you oversleep, Nozomi runs every ~10 min until noon — an 11:00 departure still makes HND by 14:15. Breathe.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate at ~162, your dollar goes far — withdraw large lump sums at 7-Eleven ATMs to minimize per-transaction fees rather than making daily small withdrawals.
December in Japan is cold, dry, and occasionally rainy. Pack versatile, thin layers (Uniqlo Heattech) and a windproof/waterproof shell rather than a heavy winter coat for temple hopping.

For a group of 8, always split into two squads of 4 for restaurants and bars — most Tokyo/Kyoto/Osaka establishments physically cannot seat 8 together, and splitting doubles your reservation success rate.
